title: Synthetic-user startup Simile raises $200M at $2B valuation 5 months after $100M Series A
slides: Can a fake user predict your real customer?
Simile just raised $200M at a $2B valuation.
Its Series A was only $100M, five months ago.
Now your A/B tests run on synthetic audiences.
Test this: run a campaign on Simile first.
thread_text:
1. Is your customer fake?

Simile just raised $200M at a $2B valuation to build synthetic audiences for your A/B tests.

2. $100M five months ago.

That Series A was followed by a $200M round — a massive bet on simulated users replacing real ones.

3. Synthetic audiences work.

Simile claims its fake users can predict real customer behavior better than traditional segments.

4. Your A/B tests now run on bots.

Instead of testing on real traffic, you simulate the reaction first — then launch to actual humans.

5. Test it this week.

Run a campaign on Simile first. If the fake user predicts the real outcome, what's the risk?
